tools.name: dex_search_contacts
tools.title: Search Contacts
tools.description: Search contacts by name, email, phone number, or any keyword. Phone numbers are matched on digits; formatting and country code are ignored (a query that is only a phone number searches phone numbers instead of the text fields, so "+420 604 354 254", "420604354254" and "604354254" all find the same contact). Use `near` (Personal Dex only) for geographic proximity ("contacts in the Bay Area", "near Sydney") — the place is geocoded and contacts are matched by their own coordinates, so it finds people whose saved location differs from the query (e.g. "San Francisco" still matches "Bay Area"). `near` and `query` combine (AND): "engineers in the Bay Area" → query "engineer" + near "Bay Area". Returns up to `limit` results. Use an empty query to list contacts sorted by most recently interacted. In a Dex for Teams workspace these rows carry no keep-in-touch cadence: read one contact's Team and My cadences with dex_get_contact, see who is due with dex_list_upcoming_reminders_and_birthdays, or select contacts by cadence with dex_filter_contacts' has_frequency (true/false; it matches Team cadences only, so a contact with only a My cadence matches false).

query.description: Search query (name, company, job title, phone number, etc.). A phone number is matched on its digits only — pass it in any formatting, with or without the country code. Use empty string to list all contacts. When `near` is set, use this ONLY for an additional non-location filter to narrow within the area (e.g. "engineer", "Google") — leave it empty for everyone nearby, and do NOT repeat the place name here (that over-filters).

near.description: Geographic proximity search: a place to find contacts near ("Bay Area", "Sydney", "Austin, TX"). Matches contacts by their coordinates within `radius_km`. tools.name: dex_get_contact
tools.title: Get Contact
tools.description: Get a single contact by ID with full details including emails, phone numbers, location (text plus latitude/longitude when geocoded), keep-in-touch cadence (`frequency` / `never_keep_in_touch` on Personal Dex; in a Dex for Teams workspace, `keep_in_touch` with the contact's Team cadence as `team` and your own My cadence as `my`, each left out or null when not set, so `keep_in_touch: {}` means the contact has neither), tags, groups, custom fields, related contacts, and optionally recent notes/timeline. Workspace connections also include `team_interactions`: up to 20 members by recency, `members_total`, and the strongest current connection (2 × meeting_count + email_count; ties or all-zero use most recent email, meeting or shared note). Counts cover all of the member's emails/meetings with the contact across connected accounts, not just shared accounts, and require active membership and current sharing for that channel. Null means unknown. Former members retain dates only and never rank strongest. The block is omitted if unavailable. Use `fields` to request only the relation data needed and keep rich contacts within the response limit.

custom_field_ids.description: Return only these custom-field value rows. Use with fields: ["contacts_custom_fields"] for the smallest response.

team_interactions.description: Workspace only. Up to 20 members by recency, with the strongest current member ranked across all members. Counts sum all connected accounts for the contact and require current channel sharing; null means unknown. Dates survive departure. Absent if the lookup failed.

tools.name: dex_complete_keep_in_touch
tools.title: Complete Keep-in-Touch
tools.description: Mark a keep-in-touch contact as done — records that the user was just in touch, so the cadence resets and the next reminder lands one frequency interval from now (the dashboard's "Mark as complete"). Pass snooze_days to instead push the next reminder out without recording a touch (the dashboard's snooze uses 7). Set or clear the cadence itself via dex_update_contact's keep_in_touch field, or dex_set_keep_in_touch for many contacts at once. In a Dex for Teams workspace it acts on the contact's Team or My cadence (pass kind when the contact has both) and returns the rescheduled `cadence`: "We met" on a Team cadence writes a note shared with the workspace, on a My cadence a private note (returned as `note_id`), and a viewer gets no note. That shared note counts as your own touch too, so marking the Team cadence done also restarts your My cadence on the contact, if you have one. A snooze only hides the cadence until it ends and never moves its due date, so one that ends on or before the next due date changes nothing and the result carries a `warning` saying so. Set or remove a workspace cadence with dex_set_keep_in_touch.

tools.name: dex_set_keep_in_touch
tools.title: Set Keep-in-Touch Cadence
tools.description: Set or clear the keep-in-touch cadence for up to 500 contacts in one call (chunk larger sets into multiple calls) — the bulk companion to dex_update_contact's keep_in_touch field. An interval sets how often to stay in touch ("7 days" = weekly, "14 days" = every 2 weeks, "1 mon" = monthly, "42 days" = every 6 weeks, "3 mons" = quarterly, "6 mons" = every 6 months, "1 year" = yearly) — this is "remind me to reach out every N", "stay in touch every N". "never" is the explicit don't-keep-in-touch mark — "no regular outreach", "stop reaching out", "don't keep in touch with them", "stop reminding me about them". "unset" simply clears the cadence so the contact has none — "no cadence", "remove the keep-in-touch" — leaving them unmarked rather than flagged. Every value overwrites whatever cadence each contact already has — and "never"/"unset" leave nothing in its place — so confirm with the user before changing a large set. Marking a due keep-in-touch as done is dex_complete_keep_in_touch, not this tool. In a Dex for Teams workspace (at most 100 contacts per call): kind is required — "team" sets the cadence shared with the whole workspace (needs write access), "my" your own private cadence — and the frequency is one of the workspace's own, chosen with exactly one of cadence (an interval must match a workspace frequency exactly; a month is 30 days, a year 365), frequency_days or frequency_id. A contact that already has a cadence of that kind moves to the new frequency, "unset" removes it, and "never" is not available. This tool never creates frequencies; an owner or admin adds them in Settings → Keep in touch.

In a Dex for Teams workspace an interval must match one of the workspace's frequencies exactly, "unset" removes the cadence of `kind`, "never" is refused, and frequency_days or frequency_id may be passed instead (exactly one of the three).

tools.title: List Upcoming Reminders, Birthdays and Keep in Touch
tools.description: What's coming up for the user inside a date window, like the Dex homepage: the contacts whose birthday falls in the window, the open reminders due in it, and the keep-in-touch contacts due for a touch by the end of it. Defaults to the next 7 days starting today — use `days: 30` for the next month, or set `from` to look at a specific week. Use this for questions like "whose birthday is next week?", "who should I reach out to this week?" or "what do I have coming up?". Recurring reminders are listed on their next occurrence. Birthdays the user already marked done this year on the homepage are omitted. `keep_in_touch` DOES include contacts already overdue for a touch (flagged `is_overdue`) — the homepage keeps showing them as due until the touch is logged. Reminders are picked by the day they come up inside the window, so reminders due before `from` are NOT included — call dex_list_reminders with is_overdue=true for those. Dates, "today" and `is_overdue` are judged in UTC, not the user's timezone: a reminder due inside the window still reads `is_overdue: true` once its day is past in UTC, as one due on `from` is when `from` is the user's local date and UTC has already reached the next day. tools.description: What's coming up for the user inside a date window, like the Dex homepage: the contacts whose birthday falls in the window, the open reminders due in it, and the keep-in-touch contacts due for a touch by the end of it. Defaults to the next 7 days starting today — use `days: 30` for the next month, or set `from` to look at a specific week. Use this for questions like "whose birthday is next week?", "who should I reach out to this week?" or "what do I have coming up?". Recurring reminders are listed on their next occurrence. Birthdays the user already marked done this year on the homepage are omitted. `keep_in_touch` DOES include contacts already overdue for a touch (flagged `is_overdue`) — the homepage keeps showing them as due until the touch is logged. Reminders are picked by the day they come up inside the window, so reminders due before `from` are NOT included — call dex_list_reminders with is_overdue=true for those. Dates, "today" and `is_overdue` are judged in UTC, not the user's timezone: a reminder due inside the window still reads `is_overdue: true` once its day is past in UTC, as one due on `from` is when `from` is the user's local date and UTC has already reached the next day. In a Dex for Teams workspace: `keep_in_touch` lists the workspace's Team cadences and your own My cadences due by the end of the window (narrow with kind; each row carries cadence_id, kind and frequency_days, and `due_on` accounts for a snooze); `reminders` are the workspace's one-off reminders (workspace reminders do not recur), across the whole workspace rather than only yours; and birthdays are not available, so `birthdays` is empty and `unavailable_in_workspace` lists it.

tools.name: dex_list_workspaces
tools.title: List Workspaces
tools.description: List the Dex for Teams workspaces the user belongs to, with their role in each and whether API & MCP access is turned on (api_access_enabled), and say where this MCP connection acts: `connection` is { kind: "personal" } for Personal Dex or { kind: "workspace", workspace_id } for a workspace, whose row is marked current: true. A connection acts in that one place only. To work somewhere else, an OAuth or device-code connection connects again and picks Personal or another workspace on the Dex consent page; an API key acts where it was created (Personal or one workspace), so use a key created for the other place in Dex under Settings → Dex API & MCP. Naming another workspace with ?workspace= is refused. A workspace only works with api_access_enabled true, which a workspace owner or admin turns on in the workspace's settings. Roles: viewer can read; standard, admin and owner can read and write, and owners and admins can also create and edit custom-field definitions over MCP. Whatever the role, a workspace connection never deletes contacts, tags, groups or custom fields, merges contacts, or runs dex_archive_contacts (any number of contacts, archive or restore): archive or restore one contact at a time with dex_update_contact is_archived, and do the rest in the Dex app.

tools.title: List Workspace Members
tools.description: List the active members of this connection's Dex for Teams workspace: member_id, name, email, role and is_you (the caller). Use a member's member_id as `assignee_id` on dex_create_reminder, dex_update_reminder and dex_list_reminders. Pass `query` (part of a name or email) to find a specific member, e.g. before assigning a reminder. Returns up to `limit` members (default 50); if `has_more` is true, pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` with the SAME `query` to continue; a new query starts without a cursor. Only active members can be assigned. Viewers can read but cannot edit or complete a reminder, so assigning one strands it; prefer owner, admin or standard members. Workspace connections only: a Personal connection has no workspace and this tool is refused.

flags.description: Mark a keep-in-touch contact as done — records that the user was just in touch, so the cadence resets and the next reminder lands one frequency interval from now (the dashboard's "Mark as complete"). Pass snooze_days to instead push the next reminder out without recording a touch (the dashboard's snooze uses 7). Set or clear the cadence itself via dex_update_contact's keep_in_touch field, or dex_set_keep_in_touch for many contacts at once. In a Dex for Teams workspace it acts on the contact's Team or My cadence (pass kind when the contact has both) and returns the rescheduled `cadence`: "We met" on a Team cadence writes a note shared with the workspace, on a My cadence a private note (returned as `note_id`), and a viewer gets no note. That shared note counts as your own touch too, so marking the Team cadence done also restarts your My cadence on the contact, if you have one. A snooze only hides the cadence until it ends and never moves its due date, so one that ends on or before the next due date changes nothing and the result carries a `warning` saying so. Set or remove a workspace cadence with dex_set_keep_in_touch.

flags.description: Archive or unarchive up to 500 contacts by ID (chunk larger sets into multiple calls). Archived contacts keep all their data (notes, reminders, history) but are hidden from the default contact list, search, and keep-in-touch reminders — the reversible alternative to dex_delete_contacts, recommended for bulk cleanup. Always show the user which contacts will be archived and get their confirmation first. Archiving MORE THAN 20 contacts in one call is server-enforced: the call is rejected (nothing changes) unless it carries confirm: true AND expected_count equal to the number of distinct contact_ids — the count the user confirmed. Restoring (archived: false) is never gated. Find archived contacts with dex_filter_contacts archived_only:true and restore them with archived:false. Not available on a Dex for Teams workspace connection: archive or restore one contact at a time with dex_update_contact is_archived (true or false). flags.description: Merge duplicate contacts. Each group of IDs is consolidated into one surviving contact — all data is combined onto it and the other IDs are deleted.
